note: Attacker-controlled bytes are wrapped in a synthetic reader and become the input source for the PKCS#15 reader path.
The first two attacker bytes determine the length of the next chunk, so later parsing decisions are fully input-driven.
The synthetic reader is connected to OpenSC, causing the Coolkey card driver to initialize card state from the fuzzed APDU stream.
Successful Coolkey initialization stores the newly allocated private state on the card, making it reachable by later teardown paths.
If initialization later fails, the same private state is freed during cleanup, so any subsequent teardown that still sees the stale pointer can free it again.
The driver's finish hook unconditionally frees the card's private state during disconnect.
The object list is iterated and each stored heap buffer is freed; if the same private state is finalized again, this becomes a double free on the same pointer.
The generic disconnect path invokes the driver's finish hook again before freeing the card, so the already-freed Coolkey private state is finalized a second time.
After the repeated finish call, the card object itself is freed, ending the lifecycle after the double-free condition has already been reached.
